ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 18555, Dec. 28, 2021, as amended), notably Articles 289, 292, 317 and 332; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 19379, Feb. 20, 2024, as amended), notably Articles 4 through 7; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 34494, Jun. 4, 2024, as amended), notably Articles 5, 8 and 9; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 19499, Dec. 31, 2023, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 17507, Oct. 1, 2020, as amended), notably Article 6; United Nations Security Council Resolutions Implementation Act (Act No. 17986, Apr. 1, 2021), notably Article 7; and the Financial Services Commission Regulations on Customer Due Diligence and Beneficial Owner Identification (FSC Decision No. 2024-45). The relevant UBO information is maintained internally by Korean banks and financial institutions and is accessible to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and law enforcement on a lawful-authority basis.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa Certificate of Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, Registry Office (Commercial Registration Division)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: for Hague Apostille Convention states, obtain the certified registry extract from the competent Korean court, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; for non-Apostille states, obtain the identical certified extract and then consular legalization through the Korean Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction where the document will be relied upon. Do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existing Corporate Registration / Subsistence Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea / National Court Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: for Apostille member states, the certified court certificate must be apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; for non-member states, the same certificate must undergo Korean consular legalization at the relevant Korean Embassy or Consulate. No document should receive both an Apostille and consular legalization in the same chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the applicant company or the incorporators before incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: the resolution or power of attorney must be executed before a Korean notary public; the notarial certificate is then presented to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an Apostille if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member, or to the Korean Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization if the destination state is not an Apostille member. These paths are alternative, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of the Korean corporation, sealed by the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: the articles are notarized by a Korean notary public, followed by Apostille issuance from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states; for non-member states, the notarized articles are submitted to the Korean Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Settlor of capital; if the reference is from a Korean bank, the branch manager of that bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: if the receiving financial institution requires legalization, the bank reference letter must be notarized and then apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states; for non-Apostille states, the notarized letter must be consular legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Some banks will waive legalization on the basis of direct KYC transmission; that waiver is an exception and not a legalization chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registry Office or local district court maintaining the corporate seal registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive paths: the seal certificate, being a public court document, is apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states; for non-Apostille states, the court certificate is submitted for consular legalization to the Korean Embassy or Consulate having territorial jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined in one sequential chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under Korean anti-money laundering standards, the newly formed Chusik Hoesa must be accepted by a bank only after (i) identification of all directors, officers, and every shareholder owning 25% or more of shares; (ii) real-time screening of those individuals against the U.S. OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK sanctions lists, Korean FIU watchlists, and the Korean autonomous financial sanctions list; (iii) enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, including Korean and foreign public officials, senior political leaders and their family members; (iv) ongoing transaction monitoring with event-triggered re-screening; and (v) filing a suspicious transaction report with the Korean Financial Information and Analysis Unit within seven calendar days whenever funds are known or suspected to be criminal proceeds. The bank will document a low-risk rating only after verifying the agencys actual commercial substance, source of funds and customer basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Internet Registry (Commercial Registry Name Search and Trade Name Reservation System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Korean corporation must be expressed in Hangul script in the registry; however, the distinctive name component may also contain Arabic numerals, English letters or Han characters where the registry database accepts them. The corporate form suffix must appear as Chusik Hoesa in Hangul. Foreign-language names are recorded as parallel trade names and do not replace the registered Korean name. The four-tier naming convention is: (i) mandatory form suffix Chusik Hoesa; (ii) distinctive unique name component; (iii) business-objective descriptor used in the articles; and (iv) parallel English or Han-transliterated name for international commercial use.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A trade name rejection is issued in writing by the registry officer. The applicant may file a written objection with the registration division of the competent district court within 14 calendar days of receipt of the rejection; the objection must attach the reserved-name receipt, a memorandum explaining why the name is not misleading, and revised articles where needed. If the court upholds the rejection, the applicant may institute administrative litigation before the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. If the initial reservation is valid but close to expiry, the reservation may be extended for one additional 180-day term by filing an extension application in the same internet registry portal before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Korean court registry and the National Tax Service do not accept a standalone virtual office or commercial mailbox as the registered head office. A registered address must be a physically identifiable space, occupied under a valid lease or ownership, where senior management can be reached for civil, tax, and regulatory service of process. For this advertising and app growth agency sector, a serviced office or co-working suite with a dedicated room number, physical signage and a lease agreement is acceptable; a mail-forwarding-only virtual office will be rejected at initial registration and in post-registration tax inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) new corporate business registration filing may trigger an on-location verification by the local district tax office; (2) VAT registration for digital marketing services may lead to a desk audit; (3) bank account opening under Korean CDD requires a branch visit and beneficial-owner interview; (4) municipal fire safety and workplace rules require periodic physical inspections if the address is a co-working facility; and (5) registry spot-checks may occur where the address is shared by multiple legal entities. Quantified risk: 25-35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months for a shared-office agency, increasing to 50% or more if the office cannot demonstrate actual staffing or if financial turnover appears inconsistent with the stated business scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, promulgated January 20, 1963, as amended through Act No. 19145 (2022), particularly Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 312, 317, 318, 330, 382, 389, 408 and 434; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Act No. 19708, as amended, Articles 4 and 5; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Act No. 17401, as amended, Article 18, for non-resident share subscriptions and remittances.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operating through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation), filed together with certified Articles of Incorporation, paid-in capital deposit certificate, consents of directors and auditor, and registered-office ownership or lease documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The full amount of subscribed capital must be deposited into a domestic bank account opened in the name of the company before registration, and the bank certificate of deposit must be submitted with the incorporation registration application. There is no blocked escrow account requirement under Korean law; however, the deposited capital may not be withdrawn until the registration of incorporation is completed. If non-resident founders subscribe shares and satisfy the Foreign Investment Promotion Act threshold, the foreign investment must be reported to KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank before or immediately after the share subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA, a stock corporation being incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, duly convened on [●] at [●] in Seoul, Republic of Korea.

PRESENT: The undersigned initial directors, being all of the persons entitled to attend and to vote, constituted a valid quorum and unanimously adopted the following resolutions, each to be effective upon the successful registration of incorporation.

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The Board acknowledged that the Company has authorized share capital of [●] Korean won divided into [●] ordinary shares, of which [●] shares have been subscribed by the incorporators and fully paid in cash. The Board directed the Representative Director to obtain the bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit and to attach such certificate to the application for registration of incorporation. The Board further authorized the Representative Director to complete all filings required under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for foreign currency remittances, including any foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act where applicable.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopted the registered office of the Company at [●], Republic of Korea. The Board authorized the execution of a lease agreement, service-office agreement, or owner consent document necessary to establish the registered office, and directed the Representative Director to file the exact registered address with the competent district court registration authority. 3. BANKING AND SIGNATORY AUTHORIZATION. The Board selected [●] Bank as the primary domestic banking institution and authorized the opening of corporate operating accounts, foreign-currency accounts, and any payroll or settlement accounts necessary for the Company's app growth, app store optimization, search engine optimization, localization, and digital advertising services. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution, and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Korea, with assistance from licensed corporate counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Korean attorney or notary to prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language, containing the corporate name with a Chusik Hoesa suffix, the exact business purposes covering app store optimization, search engine optimization, multilingual localization, digital marketing, advertising management, software development, consulting, and licensing of intellectual property, the total authorized capital, the number of ordinary shares, the method of incorporation, the registered office location, fiscal year, election of directors, public notice methods, and liquidation provisions. Each incorporator or a duly authorized attorney-in-fact must appear before the notary, present valid identification, execute the articles, and affix a registered seal or signature. If any incorporator is outside Korea, an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney in the Korean or English language must be submitted. After certification, the notary stamps and seals the articles, and the original must be retained for court filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identification of each incorporator
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Certificate or confirmation of corporate name availability search
Apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney for any proxy or non-resident incorporator
Proposed registered office lease agreement or owner consent form
Completed beneficial ownership identification form for anti-money-laundering compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests supplemental identity or authorization evidence, provide the original passport, apostilled power of attorney, or a notarized translation of the power of attorney. If the Articles are rejected for defective purpose clauses or missing signatures, revise the text, obtain signatures anew, and request a corrected notarial certification before proceeding to the incorporation registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-in capital and issuance of bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean domestic commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission, and a designated Foreign Exchange Bank for cross-border remittance reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation deposit account in the provisional corporate name using the certified Articles of Incorporation, the Representative Director's identification, the corporate registration preparer authorization, and bank anti-money-laundering forms. Deposit the full amount of subscribed capital in Korean won by domestic transfer or by foreign exchange remittance from a non-resident shareholder. Request the bank to issue a paid-in capital deposit certificate, balance certificate, or equivalent instrument bearing the bank seal and stating the name of the company and the amount deposited. If the shareholder is non-resident and the investment meets the Foreign Investment Promotion Act threshold, submit a foreign investment report to KOTRA or the receiving foreign exchange bank before remittance or within the statutory reporting period. The deposited funds must remain untouched until the registration of incorporation is completed by the court registry.
required_dossiers: Certified Articles of Incorporation
Identification documents of the Representative Director and shareholders
Bank-provided corporate account opening and anti-money-laundering questionnaire
Foreign exchange remittance receipt or bank wire confirmation
Source-of-funds declaration executed by the incorporators
Foreign investment report confirmation from KOTRA or foreign exchange bank, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a query regarding beneficial ownership or source of funds, respond with an organogram, certified copies of shareholder passports, and transaction histories. If a foreign remittance is blocked, obtain a corrected foreign exchange reporting code from the receiving bank or KOTRA and re-submit the remittance through the designated channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court registration of incorporation through the Internet Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office and the Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the corporate registered office, for example the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation either online through the IRO e-filing portal or directly at the court registry window. Attach the certified Articles of Incorporation, the paid-in capital deposit certificate, the incorporation minutes of the incorporators, written consents of the Representative Director and Auditor to accept appointment, documents evidencing the registered office address, the lease agreement or landlord consent, the corporate seal registration form, and the foreign investment report if a non-resident shareholder is involved. The registry verifies that all statutory formalities under Articles 295, 312, and 317 of the Commercial Act are satisfied. Upon approval, the court enters the company in the commercial registration record and issues the Certificate of Registered Corporate Facts. The legal existence of the Chusik Hoesa commences on the date of such registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Paid-in capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Minutes of the incorporation meeting or share subscription statement
Consent-to-appointment forms executed by directors and auditor
Certificate of the corporate seal specimen
Proof of registered office, such as lease agreement, owner's consent, and floor plan
Foreign investment report confirmation where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, cure each stated deficiency within the court-specified period, commonly 14 to 21 days, by filing an amended application with corrected exhibits and any additional fees. If the application is dismissed, the applicant may consult counsel, prepare a new registration packet, pay the applicable fee, and refile once the defect is fully remedied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax registration, corporate seal registration, bank activation, and statutory governance setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, competent local district tax office, the same district court registry for seal duplicate certifications, KOTRA or foreign exchange bank for foreign investment reports, and the licensed domestic bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court issues the Certificate of Registered Corporate Facts, file for the corporate Business Registration Certificate with the district tax office within the statutory window for newly established businesses, and complete the Value Added Tax and corporate income tax registrations. Register the company seal with the court and request official corporate seal certificates. Activate the temporary incorporation bank account as the permanent operating account and provide updated corporate registration documents. Prepare the shareholder registry, share ledger, board minutes book, statutory accounting records, and the corporate seal usage log. If foreign shareholders participated, file any supplemental foreign investment report and maintain evidence of compliance with Korean foreign-exchange and beneficial ownership disclosure rules. All post-incorporation contracts and client onboarding documents must identify the Chusik Hoesa registration number, registered office, and Representative Director.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Corporate Facts from the court registry
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Application form
Corporate seal and seal registration card
Identification of all directors and the Auditor
Registered office lease agreement
Bank account activation forms and final corporate bank account agreement
Foreign investment report confirmation, if non-resident shareholders are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office delays issuance of the Business Registration Certificate, file a written explanation with the court-issued registration certificate and request expedited processing. If the beneficial ownership report is rejected, correct the ownership structure description and re-file through the Financial Intelligence Unit or bank compliance officer within the applicable remedial period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of industrial, environmental, and physical licensing exemptions for a pure digital agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment, local district office, and local fire department would be the relevant authorities only if the company later adds physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, or hazardous activities; for the current ISIC 7310 digital agency scope, no industrial licensing board is engaged.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the registered business scope and determine that the company performs exclusively office-based digital services, namely app store optimization, search engine optimization, multilingual localization, digital advertising campaign management, content marketing, and related consulting. Since ISIC 7310 is a service activity and the company does not own or operate manufacturing installations, chemical facilities, assembly lines, warehouses, or pollutant-discharge points, no operating license under the Korean Industrial Development Act or sectoral licensing statute is required. Verify that the leased office is authorized for general business use and that the lessor maintains the building fire-safety completion certificate required under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control Act. If the company later adds server hardware assembly, logistics warehousing, or any physical production activity, the management must restart the licensing analysis and engage the Ministry of Environment for Environmental Impact Assessment classification at least 90 days before commencement.
required_dossiers: Corporate Business Registration Certificate
Registered office lease agreement and building fire-safety certificate
Written business scope determination memorandum prepared by counsel
Certificate of Registered Corporate Facts
Floor plan of the office premises showing office-only use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal district office or lessor questions the physical use of the premises, submit the floor plan, business registration certificate, and a counsel-prepared scope-of-business memorandum demonstrating exclusive administrative and service use. If the fire department requests an occupancy inspection, cooperate and obtain a confirmation letter before conducting client visits or storing substantial IT equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; no industrial licensing board is engaged for ISIC 7310 app store optimization and search engine optimization agency services. The company is an office-based digital service provider and does not require a municipal industrial license for manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; there is no statutory operating or manufacturing license prescribed under Korean law for ASO, SEO, multilingual localization, advertising consulting, or digital marketing services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; if a future physical project were added, the Ministry of Environment would be the central authority under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; the current pure digital and consulting activity involves no construction, land-use change, industrial facility, wastewater discharge, or pollutant-emitting installation, and therefore does not trigger a Full Environmental Impact Assessment, Prior Environmental Review, or Simplified Environmental Registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the agency produces zero industrial wastewater, zero volatile organic compound emissions, and zero hazardous waste streams. Ordinary office waste is handled under the general Wastes Control Act municipal collection regime. If the company later establishes warehousing, server assembly, or any manufacturing fixture, applicable water quality and air emission quantitative standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act and Clean Air Conservation Act must be separately permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a pure office-based digital agency; no Civil Defense fire permit or industrial workplace safety approval is required for app store optimization, search engine optimization, or localization consulting. The lessor must supply a valid fire-safety completion certificate for the office building under the Fire Prevention, Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control Act, and the company must comply with general occupational safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act concerning electrical safety, emergency exits, and ergonomic office workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS) handles customs declarations and export clearance through UNI-PASS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa at the relevant District Court and obtain the Certificate of Corporate Registration and corporate seal; 2) Within 20 days of commencement of business, file the Business Registration application with the competent NTS district tax office through HomeTax or in person; the application must include the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, Korean office lease agreement, representative identification, and, where applicable, an appointment letter for a Korean tax representative; 3) NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which simultaneously serves as the corporate tax identification number, VAT registration number, and electronic tax invoice identifier; 4) For a foreign non-resident corporation operating a Korean permanent establishment or domestic place of business, the branch/PE must apply to the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean place of business, submitting certified foreign incorporation documents, constitutional documents, board resolution establishing the Korean PE, power of attorney in favor of a resident tax representative, and evidence of the Korean fixed place of business; NTS then issues a foreign corporation business registration number; 5) A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business that nevertheless has Korean VAT or withholding filing duties must appoint a resident tax representative and obtain a foreigner taxpayer identifier before filing liabilities arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Korean Chusik Hoesa is automatically a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporation tax on worldwide income under the Corporation Tax Act. There is no check-the-box election in Korean tax law. Korean consolidated tax filing with 100 percent owned domestic subsidiaries is available under the conditions prescribed in the Corporation Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch countermeasures apply under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, but no elective entity classification is available for the Chusik Hoesa structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold. VAT registration is mandatory for all business operators from the commencement of taxable supplies. A simplified taxable person regime exists for small individual enterprises under KRW 80,000,000 of annual taxable turnover, but a Chusik Hoesa stock corporation is outside that simplified regime and is required to register for VAT without any minimum revenue threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice issuance and HomeTax transmission. The taxpayer must transmit the electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) to NTS through HomeTax, generally by the day following the invoice date. API and automated machine-to-machine filing is compulsory for larger taxpayers and available to all through the NTS HomeTax integration interface. Korea does not operate pre-issuance central real-time fiscal clearance or an anti-fraud physical stamping system; instead, NTS receives the e-tax invoice data in near real time, automatically validates and reconciles purchaser and supplier ledgers, blocks mismatched business registration numbers, and subjects late, missing, or false invoices to penalty assessment. The electronic tax invoice must contain both parties business registration numbers, supply date, item description, supply value, and VAT amount.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated when the goods are actually exported from Korea under a valid customs export declaration. Exported services, including international supply of services, app growth services, ASO, SEO localization, and other foreign currency earning services provided to non-residents, qualify for the 0 percent rate if the Korean service supplier retains contemporaneous evidence that the recipient is not a Korean resident, the service is supplied for use outside Korea, the service is actually rendered to the foreign party, and the foreign currency consideration is repatriated into Korea through a Korean foreign exchange bank or foreign exchange payment account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Export Declaration Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice and signed supply or service agreement
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or equivalent proof of physical export dispatch for goods
Foreign exchange settlement certificate or bank purchase confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank showing receipt or inward remittance of foreign currency
Service completion report and payment evidence evidencing that the overseas recipient directly paid the Korean company for exported services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may retrospectively deny the zero rate when the required export documentation and foreign exchange receipt evidence are not timely obtained, retained, and produced during audit. If zero-rating is disallowed, the VAT at the standard 10 percent rate is assessed on the supply value plus statutory interest for unfaithful returns, with additional tax penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes ranging broadly up to 40 percent for unjustified refunds or unfaithful submissions. Deliberately false export declarations or forged evidence may be criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the national tax collection period is extended to 10 years for fraudulent or willful omission cases. Failure to satisfy the foreign exchange repatriation requirement also triggers penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and is treated by NTS as conclusive evidence that the transaction did not qualify for zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, exercising delegated foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of the Republic of Korea, in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Customs Service on trade settlement and reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a quasi-liberalised current-account regime with structural capital-account controls. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, routine service income, trade settlements, and dividends are legally convertible and remittable provided the transaction is routed through a resident Korean foreign-exchange bank and the required foreign-exchange reporting is completed. Korean won is moderately internationalised; current-account convertibility is effectively full, but capital-account transactions such as borrowing, equity investment, offshore deposits, and complex hedging instruments are subject to prudential licensing, transaction ceilings, and reporting limitations. Export receipts must be collected in foreign currency through a domestic foreign-exchange bank; there is no forced surrender to the central bank, but 100% of export proceeds must be brought into the country and credited to a domestic bank account within the statutory collection deadline. Profit repatriation by foreign shareholders of a Chusik Hoesa is permitted under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act once the foreign investment has been properly registered and the remittance is supported by audited accounts, tax clearance, dividend resolution, and bank confirmation. For an SEO/ASO agency, cross-border fee receipts are current-account earnings and do not require capital-account approval, but each SWIFT MT103 must carry a valid remittance purpose code to avoid document-level AML rejection. The Korean authorities maintain a strict documentary surveillance framework for both inbound and outbound settlement, with all foreign-exchange transactions reported electronically to the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within one year from the export declaration acceptance date, extendable only with prior Bank of Korea or foreign-exchange bank approval. The full amount of service and goods export receipts must be credited to a domestic foreign-exchange bank account or converted into Korean won through a domestic bank. No mandatory conversion ratio to the central bank is imposed, but 100% of export proceeds are subject to the Korean foreign-exchange banking channel and must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Treasury Account
Foreign Currency Corporate Account and Operational Korean Won Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-contraindicated as a primary treasury rail for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Wise B2B and Payoneer are licensed as money transfer or electronic money institutions in certain overseas jurisdictions, but they are not registered in South Korea as licensed foreign-exchange brokers under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and do not hold a domestic electronic financial transaction business authorisation from the Financial Services Commission. A Korean resident corporate entity may not lawfully execute inward capital registration, tax invoice settlement, or annual foreign-exchange statement filings through an unauthorised offshore digital EMI. Such platforms can be used only as supplementary payout channels for non-Korean vendor disbursements where no domestic bank account is required, but they cannot replace a domestic Tier-1 bank for corporate treasury, FX conversion, trade settlement, or profit remittance. Any attempt to route core export service revenues through an offshore EMI would likely trigger Korean customs and central bank documentary compliance rejections and create material AML risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in a domestic Korean bank branch is mandatory for the statutory director and ultimate beneficial owners during initial account onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted for a newly formed Chusik Hoesa. The director must appear with an original corporate registration certificate, company seal certificate, business registration certificate, board resolution, shareholder register, and personal identification for a face-to-face CDD interview. After the account has been fully activated, digital channels may be used for routine transaction processing, but any change of beneficial owners or directors requires fresh physical or branch-verified KYC remediation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concealment through the Chusik Hoesa shareholding structure, especially when a foreign app-growth parent owns 100% of shares while Korean economic substance is unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Articles of Incorporation, official Korean corporate registry extract showing each shareholder's real identity and share class, a beneficial ownership declaration for every natural person with over 25% direct or indirect interest, certified passport copies of all ultimate owners, a notarised board resolution confirming the final beneficiaries, and three years of audited financial statements showing paid-in capital and share issuance history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected circular foreign-exchange flows represented as ASO/SEO revenue but channelled through overseas EMI wallets and digital advertising platforms without a traceable client ecosystem.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client service agreements and statements of work, a receipt-level aged ledger, Google Ads and Apple Search Ads performance and billing snapshots, formal payment-confirmation letters from the client's clearing bank, a breakdown of each SWIFT MT103 payment with purpose codes, invoices issued in Korean and English, and a detailed non-commingling policy executed under the Chusik Hoesa corporate account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanction, PEP, or country-level risk watch triggered by a non-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner from a jurisdiction with high money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent AML due diligence report from a recognised compliance-data provider, sanctions and PEP screening snapshots with matching source-rule indicators, proof of the director's physical presence and lawful Korean residence status, a source-of-wealth statement with supporting tax and bank records, notarised residence certificates, registered-office lease evidence in Korea, and a written explanation of the commercial nexus between the Chusik Hoesa, the directors, and the foreign beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry-specific red flag for a digital marketing agency processing high-volume cross-border funds with minimal Korean tax invoices or opaque disbursement to advertising networks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: All VAT returns including zero-rated export service Vat e-Tax Invoices, a contract binder for each advertising budget, original media-buying receipts from third-party ad networks such as Google and Apple, cleared payroll and general administrative expense reports, a licensed certified public accountant letter confirming client-fund segregation from Chusik Hoesa operating capital, and a treasury flow diagram evidencing that no client funds are commingled in the corporate bank account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions from a foreign parent or investor into the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting corporate bank to a designated foreign-currency corporate account at a Korean Tier-1 bank. The remittance reference must include the foreign-investment registration number issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a clear capital contribution purpose code, and the board resolution approving the investment. The receiving domestic bank must complete the foreign-exchange transaction report with the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System and issue a foreign-exchange certificate confirming the inflow. For paid-in capital verification, the bank must match the received amount to the share subscription certificates, the company registry filing, and the executed share subscription agreement. No more than five business days should elapse between receipt and completion of the capital verification process. Any capital contribution exceeding the registered amount requires prior and post-formation modification of the corporate registry before the bank will release funds for operational use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade and service disbursements is a secure SWIFT MT103 transfer with automatic document matching, bank-to-bank beneficiary validation, and proper remittance purpose codes. For recurring high-value ad-platform payments, the Korean treasury should utilise SWIFT gpi to provide real-time payment tracking. Commercial letters of credit are permissible only when the Chusik Hoesa acts as principal in the purchase of physical advertising media, software licences, or resale inventory that requires documentary trade terms; ordinary ASO/SEO service subscriptions are not appropriate for LC mechanics. Documentary collections on D/P or D/A terms may be used for channel partners that require the presentation of shipping, delivery, or acceptance documents before payment. All outbound disbursements to foreign vendors, app stores, advertising exchanges, and contractors must be backed by a signed invoice and an underlying agreement, with the local Korean won account used solely for conversion to USD or EUR through a permitted domestic bank transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla foreign-exchange forward contracts with a domestic Korean Tier-1 bank, supported by documentary underlying receivables or payables from the ASO/SEO service export activity.

Cross-currency swaps that exactly hedge a long-term foreign-currency liability or multi-year advertising capacity commitment, subject to Bank of Korea transaction reporting and prudential documentation.
Currency options structured by a domestic Korean foreign-exchange bank, limited to hedging existing foreign-currency cashflows and not permitted for speculative uncovered positions.
Onshore over-the-counter KRW/USD swap contracts used strictly for liquidity conversion and settlement timing alignment with actual export receipts and vendor disbursements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Regional Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year close; April 30 if the company is subject to external audit and attaches the independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfounded non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; late payment interest of 0.025% per day (annualized 9.125%); repeated delinquency may trigger enforced collection of assets, seizure, and court-ordered dissolution of a dormant company under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu Local Government (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same national corporate tax deadline rules; in practice by March 31, with April 30 extension for externally audited companies; the local surtax is 10% of national corporate tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the local surtax payable; daily delinquency charge of 0.025%; prolonged non-payment leads to seizure of local immovable assets and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Certified Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART Electronic Disclosure System; simultaneously attached to the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Independent auditor's report must be submitted to the FSS within two weeks after approval by the annual shareholders' meeting, and in no case later than April 30 of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or false submission under the External Audit Act triggers administrative fines up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,850), criminal penalties for fraud, and suspension from DART disclosure for listed issuers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (DART) or a nationally designated daily economic newspaper
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year-end (April 30 for calendar-year corporations) where the Commercial Act thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or false public announcement results in a petty fine of up to KRW 2 million (approx. USD 1,540); non-compliance with disclosure can invalidate exculpatory resolutions of the shareholders' meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Records and Statutory Minute Book Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; the minute book is retained at the registered office and must be produced to the Court Registry on prior request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting must be convoked by March 31 for a calendar-year fiscal close; financial statements must be approved within three months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director who fails to convene the annual meeting is subject to a criminal fine up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,850); repeated failure may expose the director to shareholder petitions for judicial convocation and dismissal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register and Registered Office Annual Confirmation / Change Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no annual renewal registration in Korea; nonetheless, all changes in registered office, representative director, capital, or extraordinary shareholding matters must be filed within three weeks of the triggering event; annual internal calendar review is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-registration of changes makes the change ineffective against third-party bona fide purchasers and subjects the director to periodical overdue penalties; a company that ceases business entirely may face strike-off by judicial dissolution after one year of inactivity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (주식회사 등의 외부감사에 관한 법률), an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory when any of the following quantitative triggers is met at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end: (i) total assets exceed KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.7 million at KRW 1,300 = USD 1.00); (ii) total assets exceed KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.4 million) and total liabilities exceed KRW 5 billion (approx. USD 3.8 million); (iii) total assets exceed KRW 3 billion (approx. USD 2.3 million) and average number of employees exceeds 300; (iv) the entity is a listed company or is designated by the Financial Services Commission; (v) the entity qualifies as a large enterprise under the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act. Even when not exceeding these asset/headcount thresholds, any company conducting an initial public offering, seeking listing, or voluntarily adopting K-IFRS must obtain the statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies and for all statutory-audit companies above the asset threshold. Entities below the audit threshold and non-public small and medium enterprises may apply the Korean SME Accounting Standards (기업회계기준). Filing under a different GAAP is not admissible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not operate a recurring annual UBO registration for domestic unlisted stock corporations. However, under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and AML/CDD rules, the company must annually disclose to its foreign-exchange banking partners (including Wise and Payoneer) the natural persons holding or controlling 25% or more of equity, together with any capital-transfer events. As a matter of secretarial governance, the board is required to maintain an annual UBO verification pack at the registered office and present it to the statutory auditor upon request. Any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within one business day and, if it alters the registered capital or number of issued shares, reported to the Commercial Registry within three weeks. The 30-day reporting window is not applicable to ordinary Korean private stock corporations except for foreign-investment notifications to the Ministry of Economy and Finance when the receipt of foreign equity exceeds KRW 100 million.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,800 (annual registered-office legal associate fee, corporate secretarial support, and statutory filing service, depending on the city and complexity)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 (customary CPA audit fee for a mid-sized Chusik Hoesa app-growth agency exceeding the mandatory audit threshold; excludes late-filing penalties)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on the next portion up to KRW 20 billion, 21% on the next portion up to KRW 300 billion, 24% above KRW 300 billion, plus a local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of national corporate tax, making the maximum combined headline rate 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D expense tax credit up to 50% for eligible small and medium-sized enterprises under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act Article 9; corporate tax reduction of 50% for five to seven years for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in free trade or foreign investment zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; SME investment and job creation credits; no general patent box for an advertising agency.
